mi_boot_camp_humiliation.text: Day three of boot camp. You are made to apologise to a fire hydrant for 'insubordinate posture'. Everyone watches.

outcomes.laughs: The platoon laughs. Even the sergeant's moustache twitches.
outcomes.punished: Fifty push-ups and a lecture on tone.

mi_drill_sergeant.text: Sergeant Hale inspects your bunk. A coin bounces off the sheets. Another follows. A third hits your shoe, and a part of you.

mi_barracks_prank.text: Someone stuffs your boots with shaving foam. The barracks goes silent, waiting to see who you pick as culprit.

outcomes.fight: A sweaty scuffle. The sergeant breaks it up with delight.
outcomes.right: You nail the culprit. Respect restored.

mi_promotion_board.text: Promotion board. Three officers, a clipboard and a question: 'What is your biggest weakness?' You have seventeen answers.

outcomes.promoted: New stripes. Nobody sews them on right.
outcomes.flop: He hates flattery. His hobby is exposing it.

mi_deployment_orders.text: The envelope is thin but heavy. Deployment. Six months, a country you can't pronounce, and a mandatory video about sunscreen.

outcomes.exempt: A doctor signs. Your conscience does not.
outcomes.caught: The doctor sees through you. Off you go.

mi_ambush.text: The convoy slows. A road, a ridge, and the sound you'd hoped to never learn the pitch of.

outcomes.hold: You hold. Nobody ever really tells you how long it lasted.
outcomes.wounded: A fragment finds your leg. You hear yourself shouting from far away.
outcomes.serious: Medevac. Three weeks of white ceilings.
outcomes.dead: The road keeps one of you. Today, you.

mi_mine_scare.text: You spot a bump in the road and the engineer says 'don't move'. The sound of a boot lifting from a mine is silence.

outcomes.safe: Defused. He tips his helmet. You grip a canteen like a lifeline.
outcomes.dead: There isn't even time to be afraid.

mi_local_kid.text: A kid with a missing front tooth follows your patrol, selling warm soda. He says the price is 'American'. It is one dollar.

mi_mail_spouse.text: A package from {{name}}: socks, chocolate and a drawing of the dog. Under the chocolate, a letter that smells like home.

mi_mail_partner.text: A letter from {{name}}, scented. Your bunkmates read the first line over your shoulder and start making noises.

mi_mail_mother.text: {{name}} sends cookies, forty of them, each wrapped in a note that says 'Eat'. Half arrive as crumbs. They taste like Sunday.

mi_medal.text: You carried a wounded soldier across forty metres of open ground. A general with a very shiny chest wants to pin something on yours.

mi_ptsd_seed.text: A door slams in the mess tent and your whole body is on the floor before your mind arrives. You laugh about it, loudly.

outcomes.depressed: The nightmares start two weeks later.

mi_ptsd_nightmares.text: You wake up swinging for the third night in a row. The kid in the next bunk has taken to sleeping with his boots on.

outcomes.worse: It doesn't pass. It moves in.

mi_awol_temptation.text: You've got a bus ticket, a cousin's couch and a very strong feeling you could simply not be here. AWOL is a short word for a long sentence.

outcomes.caught: Military police find you in a diner, mid-pancake.

mi_reservist_callup.text: Your reserve unit calls. Thirty days, no pay worth the word, and your boss is delighted to learn you will be absent.

outcomes.fined: Fine, warning, and a stern letter.

mi_unit_buddy.text: A guy named Ortega stole your last cigarette and then your last doubt. You can tell he'll be around for decades.

mi_end_of_service.text: Your discharge paperwork arrives. Four pages, a handshake and a pin. Strange how heavy a small piece of metal can be.

mi_veteran_benefits.text: The veterans' office mails you a thick envelope: education credit, a medical card and a flag nobody asked you to fold.

mi_rifle_inspection.text: Rifle inspection. The lieutenant pulls one cleaning rag from your barrel and holds it up like a verdict.

outcomes.extra: Extra duty: cleaning every rifle in the company.

mi_field_exercise.text: Twelve-kilometre march in full pack. At kilometre eight your feet file a formal complaint.

outcomes.lucky: Nobody notices. You wave at the stragglers.
outcomes.caught: A corporal catches you. Midnight latrine duty.

mi_leave_home.text: Seventy-two hours of leave. You step off the train and your mother hugs you like you're a casserole she's afraid of dropping.

mi_fitness_test.text: Annual fitness test. The instructor holds the clipboard like a hostage. Your run-time is a matter of national pride, or something.

outcomes.top: A personal best. A medic hands you a banana.

mi_officer_candidate.text: A major takes you aside. 'The army needs leaders. You are not a leader. But you might become something near enough.'

outcomes.rejected: Rejected. 'Lacks vision', says the form, in pen.

mi_friendly_fire.text: A flare, a shout, and rounds hiss past your tent. Someone on the far ridge has a very poor map.

outcomes.stop: You stop it before anyone dies. Your hands shake for an hour.

mi_convoy_breakdown.text: Your truck dies in the middle of nowhere. The mechanic swears at it in four languages. The desert is very large and very quiet.

outcomes.fixed: The engine coughs awake. You cheer like children.
outcomes.burn: A hose bursts. Your forearm is now an educational burn.

mi_field_hospital.text: A field medic stitches you up while telling a long story about a goat. You decide not to ask what the goat did.

mi_vet_reunion.text: Ten years since discharge. Your old unit meets at a bar that smells like old ammo. Ortega is bald and happy.

mi_barracks_gambling.text: A card game starts in the back of the barracks. The stakes are cigarettes, favours and, tonight, your next three paychecks.

outcomes.win: You walk away richer and slightly hated.
outcomes.lose: You lose every cent. Your bunkmate sends flowers, as a joke.

mi_moral_order.text: An order comes down that makes your stomach turn: clear a village on thin evidence. The captain does not look at you when he says it.

outcomes.honoured: The captain, quietly, agrees. The order evaporates.
outcomes.martial: A tribunal. Your conscience goes with you.

mi_barracks_romance.text: Someone from the signal corps keeps leaving you spare batteries and a very specific look. This is how everything begins here.

outcomes.fling: A secret romance, discovered by everyone within the week.
outcomes.rebuffed: They only wanted you to have batteries.

mi_night_watch.text: Night watch. Four hours, one flask of cold coffee and a sky so full of stars it seems rude to have a rifle under it.

outcomes.ok: The only thing you miss is half an hour.
outcomes.caught: The officer on rounds files this under: tragic.

mi_supply_theft.text: Pallets of ration bars disappear from the depot overnight. Somebody in your squad is suddenly the richest man in the camp.

outcomes.rich: You sell chocolate to your own officers.
outcomes.court: The MPs have a spreadsheet. You are on it.

mi_conscript_dread.text: You never signed up. The letter had a date and no question mark. Everyone around you seems to remember the oath better than you do.

mi_officer_orders.text: As an officer, you now say 'Carry on' with such confidence that people continue to carry on, even when you meant something else.

mi_insubordination.text: Your sergeant calls your grandmother 'a frail excuse for a woman' in front of the platoon. Everyone looks at you.

outcomes.respect: The sergeant, bleeding, smiles. Strange men.

mi_base_party.text: A birthday on base, a keg of unknown origin, and a private singing a song about his hometown, which does not exist.

outcomes.legend: A legend is born. The hangover too.
outcomes.busted: Dawn arrives with a captain and a clipboard.

mi_survival_course.text: Survival course: three days, a knife and a map. The instructor says 'Eat what the earth gives you.' The earth gives you beetles.

outcomes.pass: You come back thin, proud and strangely enlightened.
outcomes.sick: A beetle was not worth it.

mi_dear_john.text: A letter from {{name}}, one paragraph long. It starts: 'I need to tell you something and I hope you can forgive me.'

mi_veteran_nightmare.text: Fireworks in July. You're under the table with the dog before you realise. The dog, to its credit, is also there.

outcomes.ok: You drink some water. It passes.
outcomes.worse: It comes back at night. And in the supermarket.
